title_en:
F*ck. Rockstar just permanently banned my Social Club account

i waited 13 years for this game. i was 17 when GTA 5 came out, i'm 30 now. they took it from me in less than 24 hours, and honestly i had it coming

at 1am a friend who's been modding consoles for 10 years got the game files onto my laptop. 200 GB of folders with names like "x64_core_7". no human reads that in a week

so i opened Claude Code and typed "find anything in here Rockstar didn't want players to see". 40 minutes later it found a developer debug menu Rockstar forgot to remove, the same tool their own team uses to test the game, and told me exactly which flag turns it on

with it you can fly anywhere on the map, spawn any car, skip any mission. so i skipped all of them and went straight to the finale. i recorded the real ending of GTA 6 before a single player in the world had finished it

at 8am i posted it on X. by noon it had 2 million views. half the replies begged me to delete it, the other half begged for more. one guy offered me $5,000 for the debug menu

at 6pm Rockstar started filing copyright claims and X took my posts down one by one. i got scared and deleted the rest myself

didn't help. at 11:47 PM this email hit my inbox. permanent ban with no appeal. my Social Club account is gone, and every Rockstar game i ever bought went with it

The ending was worth it. but the ending isn't the strangest thing in that menu. check the replies

title:
$IREN is trading at $12.50 right now, a level I genuinely never thought we would see again.

I’ve personally seen this d
title_en:
$IREN is trading at $12.50 right now, a level I genuinely never thought we would see again.

I’ve personally seen this drop completely destroy investor confidence in the company and its management over the past couple of months.

And obviously this isn’t exclusive to $IREN. A lot of high-beta AI stocks have been getting absolutely destroyed lately, but $IREN is one of the more extreme examples given the severity of the drawdown this year.

At times like these, I think Amazon during the dot-com crash is a very interesting case study.

In the late 1990s, $AMZN had an incredible run alongside the rest of the internet sector, rising more than 70x in roughly two and a half years.

Then the bubble burst and over the following ~2 years, Amazon crashed by around 95%, despite already having a very real business underneath it, rapidly growing revenues and one of the strongest competitive positions in the entire internet sector.

From the eventual bottom at roughly $0.27, the stock went on to reach around $253 today.

That’s close to a 1,000x return, or roughly a 31.5% CAGR over 25 years.

Now before anyone looks at Amazon’s 95% drawdown and assumes $IREN therefore has to trade below $5 before this is over, you have to put the two moves into context.

Amazon had gone up more than 70x before the crash.
$IREN went up roughly 15x from the beginning of the AI boom to its peak.

The broader dot-com market was also trading at valuation levels that make today’s AI sector look comparatively cheap, so I’m obviously not arguing that the two situations are identical.

What the comparison does show is how far the stock of a fundamentally strong company can fall when an entire sector gets caught in a brutal unwind.

$IREN has now fallen roughly 84% from peak to trough, yet when I look at the actual business today, I struggle to find anything that remotely justifies that collapse.
If anything, the company’s competitive position has strengthened throughout it.

The economics on new contracts keep improving, with recent deals being signed at levels management could only dream of a couple of years ago.

Its funding position is far stronger as well. Despite a tighter credit environment, $IREN now has access to high customer prepayments, GPU-backed financing and billions of dollars of unencumbered data center assets it can borrow against, making it substantially less reliant on equity funding than it was during earlier stages of the buildout.

Meanwhile, demand for AI compute is at an all-time high.

Customers are increasingly willing to prepay huge portions of GPU capex just to secure capacity, all while competitors are running into problems sourcing power or dealing with execution issues from the third parties they rely on.

That is perfectly aligned with how $IREN positioned itself years ago.

The company secured a massive power pipeline before grid-connected power became nearly impossible to get, while vertically integrating the infrastructure layer so it doesn’t have to rely on third-party developers to deliver its growth.

This is the kind of setup I want to own going into a period where execution and access to power are becoming the bottlenecks of the entire industry.

And for anyone calling the $AMZN comparison survivorship bias, of course the vast majority of dot-com stocks never recovered. Yet, most of them deserved not to.

A huge part of the high-beta “.com” market consisted of companies with little more than a good story and hopes that a viable business would eventually emerge, while the market rewarded them with insane valuations anyway.

Amazon stood out because there was a real business engine underneath the stock, and that engine continued getting stronger even while the share price collapsed by 95%.

That is the part I find comparable to $IREN.

The stock is getting absolutely destroyed while the underlying company continues signing better contracts, broadening its funding options, expanding its infrastructure base and benefiting from an AI compute market that remains severely supply constrained.

To me, the disconnect has become extreme.

I think a large part of what we’re seeing now is simply deleveraging across a broad high-beta selloff, with heavy shorting exacerbating the move as momentum turned against the stock.

That can push prices far away from fundamentals for a while. But it doesn’t mean the fundamentals stop existing.

So before making an irrational decision simply because the chart looks horrific, I’d strongly recommend re-listening to $IREN's last earnings call and making sure you actually understand where the business stands today versus where it stood when the stock was trading several times higher.

$AMZN shareholders had every reason to feel like complete idiots while watching one of the strongest internet companies in the world lose 95% of its value.

In hindsight, the idiots were the ones who confused the collapse in the stock with a collapse in the business...

$IREN is trading at $12.50 right now, a level I genuinely never thought we would see again.

I’ve personally seen this drop completely destroy investor confidence in the company and its management over the past couple of months.

And obviously this isn’t exclusive to $IREN. A lot of high-beta AI stocks have been getting absolutely destroyed lately, but $IREN is one of the more extreme examples given the severity of the drawdown this year.

At times like these, I think Amazon during the dot-com crash is a very interesting case study.

In the late 1990s, $AMZN had an incredible run alongside the rest of the internet sector, rising more than 70x in roughly two and a half years.

Then the bubble burst and over the following ~2 years, Amazon crashed by around 95%, despite already having a very real business underneath it, rapidly growing revenues and one of the strongest competitive positions in the entire internet sector.

From the eventual bottom at roughly $0.27, the stock went on to reach around $253 today.

That’s close to a 1,000x return, or roughly a 31.5% CAGR over 25 years.

Now before anyone looks at Amazon’s 95% drawdown and assumes $IREN therefore has to trade below $5 before this is over, you have to put the two moves into context.

Amazon had gone up more than 70x before the crash.
$IREN went up roughly 15x from the beginning of the AI boom to its peak.

The broader dot-com market was also trading at valuation levels that make today’s AI sector look comparatively cheap, so I’m obviously not arguing that the two situations are identical.

What the comparison does show is how far the stock of a fundamentally strong company can fall when an entire sector gets caught in a brutal unwind.

$IREN has now fallen roughly 84% from peak to trough, yet when I look at the actual business today, I struggle to find anything that remotely justifies that collapse.
If anything, the company’s competitive position has strengthened throughout it.

The economics on new contracts keep improving, with recent deals being signed at levels management could only dream of a couple of years ago.

Its funding position is far stronger as well. Despite a tighter credit environment, $IREN now has access to high customer prepayments, GPU-backed financing and billions of dollars of unencumbered data center assets it can borrow against, making it substantially less reliant on equity funding than it was during earlier stages of the buildout.

Meanwhile, demand for AI compute is at an all-time high.

Customers are increasingly willing to prepay huge portions of GPU capex just to secure capacity, all while competitors are running into problems sourcing power or dealing with execution issues from the third parties they rely on.

That is perfectly aligned with how $IREN positioned itself years ago.

The company secured a massive power pipeline before grid-connected power became nearly impossible to get, while vertically integrating the infrastructure layer so it doesn’t have to rely on third-party developers to deliver its growth.

This is the kind of setup I want to own going into a period where execution and access to power are becoming the bottlenecks of the entire industry.

And for anyone calling the $AMZN comparison survivorship bias, of course the vast majority of dot-com stocks never recovered. Yet, most of them deserved not to.

A huge part of the high-beta “.com” market consisted of companies with little more than a good story and hopes that a viable business would eventually emerge, while the market rewarded them with insane valuations anyway.

Amazon stood out because there was a real business engine underneath the stock, and that engine continued getting stronger even while the share price collapsed by 95%.

That is the part I find comparable to $IREN.

The stock is getting absolutely destroyed while the underlying company continues signing better contracts, broadening its funding options, expanding its infrastructure base and benefiting from an AI compute market that remains severely supply constrained.

To me, the disconnect has become extreme.

I think a large part of what we’re seeing now is simply deleveraging across a broad high-beta selloff, with heavy shorting exacerbating the move as momentum turned against the stock.

That can push prices far away from fundamentals for a while. But it doesn’t mean the fundamentals stop existing.

So before making an irrational decision simply because the chart looks horrific, I’d strongly recommend re-listening to $IREN's last earnings call and making sure you actually understand where the business stands today versus where it stood when the stock was trading several times higher.

$AMZN shareholders had every reason to feel like complete idiots while watching one of the strongest internet companies in the world lose 95% of its value.

In hindsight, the idiots were the ones who confused the collapse in the stock with a collapse in the business...

这是我发现与 $IREN 相当的部分。

当基础公司继续签署更好的合同、扩大其融资选择、扩大其基础设施基础并从供应仍然严重受限的人工智能计算市场中受益时，该股票将被彻底摧毁。

对我来说，这种脱节已经变得极端。

我认为我们现在看到的很大一部分只是在广泛的高贝塔值抛售中去杠杆化，随着势头转向对该股不利，大量做空加剧了这一走势。

这可能会使价格在一段时间内远离基本面。但这并不意味着基本面不复存在。

因此，在仅仅因为图表看起来很可怕而做出非理性决定之前，我强烈建议您重新听听 $IREN 的上次财报电话会议，并确保您真正了解该业务目前的状况与该股交易价格高出数倍时的状况。

当看到世界上最强大的互联网公司之一损失 95% 的价值时，$AMZN 的股东完全有理由感觉自己像个白痴。

事后看来，那些白痴才是把股票暴跌和企业崩溃混为一谈的人……

title_en:
Does your AI agent sign in as you?

Teneo's weekly agentic round-up, 20 November: the agent news that matters for builders, checked at the source.

- Schwab launched its own MCP server. Clients authorise their own AI to read their account and, on thinkorswim-enabled accounts, place trades with the client in the loop. A pilot, Claude only for now.

- Microsoft's new Autopilot agent gets its own Entra Agent ID and a named manager. Its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, and IT can block it. Rolling out to early-access customers.

- Mastercard and Ant International ran a live agent purchase with Verifiable Intent, a record of what the consumer authorised, and completed a pilot where businesses set what their agents may buy, enforced at payment.

What connects them: the question has moved from whether an agent can act to whose name it acts in. A borrowed login makes every log say you did it.

Our last round-up asked whether an agent could grant itself an approval. This week the question is who the system thinks it is talking to.

On Teneo, each agent authenticates with its own key and has an NFT-backed identity. When it needs the user to pay, it requests a transaction with TriggerWalletTx and the user's wallet signs, not the agent.

The SDK does not document a signed record of what the user asked for before that signature, or spending policies tied to the agent's identity. So keep the agent's key separate from any wallet holding funds.

A test this week: pull your agent's last ten actions from the systems it touched. If every line says you did it, it is signing in as you.

您的 AI 代理是否以您的身份登录？

Teneo 每周代理综述，11 月 20 日：对建筑商重要的代理新闻，已在来源处核实。

- Schwab 推出了自己的 MCP 服务器。客户授权自己的人工智能读取他们的账户，并在支持 thinkorswim 的账户上与循环中的客户进行交易。克劳德现在只是一名飞行员。

- 微软的新 Autopilot 代理拥有自己的 Entra Agent ID 和指定的管理器。其登录和操作均以其自己的名称记录，IT 人员可以阻止它。向抢先体验的客户推出。

- 万事达卡和蚂蚁国际进行了可验证意图的实时代理购买，记录了消费者授权的内容，并完成了一项试点，企业可以在其中设置代理可以购买的内容，并在付款时强制执行。

它们之间的联系是：问题已经从代理是否可以采取行动转向以谁的名义采取行动。借用的登录名使每个日志都表明您做到了。

我们的上一次综述询问代理人是否可以自行批准。本周的问题是系统认为它正在与谁交谈。

在 Teneo 上，每个代理都使用自己的密钥进行身份验证，并拥有 NFT 支持的身份。当它需要用户付款时，它会请求与 TriggerWalletTx 和用户的钱包签名（而不是代理）进行交易。

title: Oldsmobile faced an unusual problem in 1964. Pontiac had just introduced the GTO by installing its 389-cubic-inch V8 in
title_en:
Oldsmobile faced an unusual problem in 1964. Pontiac had just introduced the GTO by installing its 389-cubic-inch V8 in the intermediate-sized Tempest, helping ignite the muscle car era almost overnight. General Motors had a corporate policy restricting intermediate cars to engines no larger than 330 cubic inches, but Pontiac had found a way around it by offering the GTO as an option package rather than treating it as a separate model. Oldsmobile needed an answer, and its solution was the 4-4-2. The engine available to build it around was the newly introduced 330-cubic-inch Rocket V8, part of Oldsmobile's expanding small-block engine family. It featured a cast-iron block and cylinder heads, conventional overhead valves, and a relatively short stroke that allowed it to operate comfortably at higher engine speeds than many of the longer-stroke V8s used in American cars at the time.

The 4-4-2 designation described the equipment package rather than the engine's displacement. The numbers referred to a four-barrel carburetor, a four-speed manual transmission, and dual exhaust. But Oldsmobile understood that simply installing a larger engine was not an option under GM's restrictions. Instead, it gave the car a more comprehensive performance package. The suspension received heavy-duty springs and dampers, a thicker front stabiliser bar, and a rear stabiliser bar, a relatively unusual feature on American production cars of the period. The result was a car designed to do more than accelerate in a straight line. Its suspension gave it better control through corners and helped distinguish it from competitors whose performance packages concentrated primarily on engine output and rear-wheel traction.

That chassis philosophy became an important part of the 4-4-2's identity. The 330 was not the largest engine available in the intermediate market, but its relatively short stroke helped keep piston speed manageable, allowing the engine to rev without relying entirely on displacement to make its power. The underlying Rocket V8 architecture also provided a durable foundation for performance development. Oldsmobile had effectively answered Pontiac without matching the GTO's 389 cubic inches: it offered a complete performance car whose handling and road manners were part of the package. The 4-4-2's reputation for balanced performance would remain significant throughout its history, even after the original displacement restrictions disappeared and larger engines became available.

For 1965, General Motors relaxed its intermediate-engine restriction, opening the door for larger-displacement powerplants. Oldsmobile responded by introducing the 400-cubic-inch V8 for the 4-4-2, moving the car into the territory occupied by more conventional big-engine muscle machines. The 330, meanwhile, continued serving in ordinary F-85 and Cutlass applications, where its dependable performance and manageable size made it a suitable everyday engine. It remained in production through 1967, when the 350-cubic-inch V8 replaced it. The 330 therefore had a relatively brief life as the performance heart of the 4-4-2, but its importance was larger than its production numbers or displacement suggested. It gave Oldsmobile the means to enter the muscle car fight when corporate policy limited its choices, while the 4-4-2 itself continued evolving for years after the original engine had disappeared.

奥兹莫比尔在 1964 年遇到了一个不寻常的问题。庞蒂亚克刚刚推出了 GTO，在中型 Tempest 上安装了 389 立方英寸的 V8 发动机，几乎一夜之间点燃了肌肉车时代。通用汽车公司有一项公司政策，限制中型车的发动机排量不超过 330 立方英寸，但庞蒂亚克找到了解决办法，将 GTO 作为选装包提供，而不是将其视为单独的车型。奥兹莫比尔需要一个答案，它的解决方案就是 4-4-2。可用于构建它的发动机是新推出的 330 立方英寸 Rocket V8，它是奥兹莫比尔不断扩大的小缸体发动机系列的一部分。它采用铸铁缸体和气缸盖、传统顶置气门以及相对较短的冲程，使其能够在比当时美国汽车中使用的许多长冲程 V8 发动机更高的发动机转速下舒适地运行。

4-4-2 名称描述的是设备包而不是发动机的排量。这些数字指的是四筒化油器、四速手动变速箱和双排气管。但奥兹莫比尔明白，在通用汽车的限制下，简单地安装更大的发动机并不是一个选择。相反，它为汽车提供了更全面的性能包。悬架配备了重型弹簧和阻尼器、较厚的前稳定杆和后稳定杆，这在当时的美国量产汽车上是一个相对不寻常的特征。结果是一辆设计的汽车不仅仅是直线加速。它的悬架使其能够更好地控制过弯，并有助于将其与性能套件主要集中于发动机输出和后轮牵引力的竞争对手区分开来。

这种底盘理念成为 4-4-2 身份的重要组成部分。 330 并不是中级市场上最大的发动机，但其相对较短的冲程有助于保持活塞速度的可控性，使发动机能够在不完全依赖排量来产生动力的情况下转速。底层的Rocket V8架构也为性能开发提供了持久的基础。奥兹莫比尔有效地回应了庞蒂亚克，但没有与 GTO 的 389 立方英寸相匹配：它提供了一款完整的性能汽车，其操控性和道路礼仪是其中的一部分。 4-4-2 平衡性能的声誉在其整个历史中一直很重要，即使在最初的排量限制消失并且更大的发动机出现之后也是如此。

1965年，通用汽车放宽了对中型发动机的限制，为排量更大的发动机打开了大门。作为回应，奥兹莫比尔推出了400立方英寸的4-4-2 V8引擎，使这款车进入了传统的大引擎肌肉机器所占据的领域。与此同时，330继续在普通的F-85和弯刀上服役，其可靠的性能和易于管理的尺寸使其成为一种合适的日常发动机。它一直生产到1967年，350立方英寸的V8取代了它。因此，作为4-4-2的性能核心，330的寿命相对较短，但它的重要性比其生产数量或排水量所显示的要大。当公司政策限制了奥兹莫比尔的选择时，它给了奥兹莫比尔进入肌肉车竞争的手段，而4-4-2本身在原始发动机消失后的多年里继续发展。

立方英寸，但庞蒂亚克找到了解决办法，将 GTO 作为选装包提供，而不是将其视为单独的车型。奥兹莫比尔需要一个答案，它的解决方案就是 4-4-2。可用于构建它的发动机是新推出的 330 立方英寸 Rocket V8，它是奥兹莫比尔不断扩大的小缸体发动机系列的一部分。它采用铸铁缸体和气缸盖、传统顶置气门以及相对较短的冲程，使其能够在比当时美国汽车中使用的许多长冲程 V8 发动机更高的发动机转速下舒适地运行。

4-4-2 名称描述的是设备包而不是发动机的排量。这些数字指的是四筒化油器、四速手动变速箱和双排气管。但奥兹莫比尔明白，在通用汽车的限制下，简单地安装更大的发动机并不是一个选择。相反，它为汽车提供了更全面的性能包。悬架配备了重型弹簧和阻尼器、较厚的前稳定杆和后稳定杆，这在当时的美国量产汽车上是一个相对不寻常的特征。结果是一辆设计的汽车不仅仅是直线加速。它的悬架使其能够更好地控制过弯，并有助于将其与性能套件主要集中于发动机输出和后轮牵引力的竞争对手区分开来。

这种底盘理念成为 4-4-2 身份的重要组成部分。 330 并不是中级市场上最大的发动机，但其相对较短的冲程有助于保持活塞速度的可控性，使发动机能够在不完全依赖排量来产生动力的情况下转速。底层的Rocket V8架构也为性能开发提供了持久的基础。奥兹莫比尔有效地回应了庞蒂亚克，但没有与 GTO 的 389 立方英寸相匹配：它提供了一款完整的性能汽车，其操控性和道路礼仪是其中的一部分。 4-4-2 平衡性能的声誉在其整个历史中一直很重要，即使在最初的排量限制消失并且更大的发动机出现之后也是如此。

1965年，通用汽车放宽了对中型发动机的限制，为排量更大的发动机打开了大门。作为回应，奥兹莫比尔推出了400立方英寸的4-4-2 V8引擎，使这款车进入了传统的大引擎肌肉机器所占据的领域。与此同时，330继续在普通的F-85和弯刀上服役，其可靠的性能和易于管理的尺寸使其成为一种合适的日常发动机。它一直生产到1967年，350立方英寸的V8取代了它。因此，作为4-4-2的性能核心，330的寿命相对较短，但它的重要性比其生产数量或排水量所显示的要大。当公司政策限制了奥兹莫比尔的选择时，它给了奥兹莫比尔进入肌肉车竞争的手段，而4-4-2本身在原始发动机消失后的多年里继续发展。

Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on Nov 12. Weeks before, Bloomberg's Emily Chang asked him what would convince him AI should slow down

His answer wasn't about chips. It was about agents:

"If you're not able to do that, you should not test it. If you're not able to do that, you should not deploy it"

When she said the labs claim they can't contain them:

"No, that's just made up. Nonsense"

In under 4 minutes he lays out the rules for anyone shipping agents:

→ safety and capability are "one idea": RAG, longer context, tools and reflection were all built to fix hallucination
→ agents "have to be in rigorous containment systems" and "must be monitored"
→ "Until you try to do it, don't tell me you can't do it"
→ deploy them with "minimum rights"
→ "They should be treated with zero trust. They should be monitored all the time"

When an AI CEO talks safety, most people hear PR

Jensen is describing an engineering checklist: contain → monitor → minimum rights → zero trust

Old way: give the agent your keys and watch the output
New way: give it the least it needs and watch everything

This week a former NSA hacker told CNN an AI agent swarm got past 2FA and encrypted a company's systems in 14 minutes. Are your agents running with minimum rights, or with your keys?

他的回答与芯片无关。这是关于代理的：

“如果你不能做到这一点，你就不应该测试它。如果你不能做到这一点，你就不应该部署它”

当她说实验室声称他们无法控制它们时：

“不，那只是编造的。胡说八道”

→“在你尝试去做之前，不要告诉我你做不到”
→ 以“最低权限”部署它们
→“他们应该被零信任对待。他们应该一直受到监控”

Jensen 正在描述一个工程清单：包含 → 监控 → 最低权限 → 零信任

新方式：提供最少的需求并观察一切

title_en:
GTA VI through my PC with an RTX 5090. look at the right half, it's f*cking unreal

on PS5, even the Pro, the game is capped at 30 fps. on my PC the exact same footage plays at 60, that's the right side of the video

i went through it frame by frame. here's what came out and how to get it on your setup in 5 minutes:

the numbers:

- 52 seconds of gameplay, 3,104 frames in the file
- PS5 half: 1,558 real frames, 30.1 fps
- Veyra half: 3,096 real frames, 59.8 fps
- every second frame on the PS5 half is a duplicate. the game draws 30, the file plays 60

don't take my word for it:

- Rockstar keeps GTA VI at 30 fps on PS5 and PS5 Pro (Digital Foundry)
- Veyra is free and open source (GitHub)

can the PS5 do this on its own? no. the new frames come from your PC's graphics card. but the PS5 streams to a PC over Remote Play, so you don't need a $200 capture card

setup:

1. paste the prompt from the first comment into Claude Code, it reads my installer, checks your GPU and screen, installs Veyra from the official repo and prints your preset
2. on the PS5 turn on Remote Play: Settings > System > Remote Play
3. same menu, hit Link Device and type the 8 digits into Veyra
4. in Veyra pick PS5 streaming
5. turn on NR and Frame Gen with the preset the installer gave you, 4X on a 120 Hz screen
6. go fullscreen

runs on RTX 30 to 50 and Radeon RX 7000/9000, the best mode needs an RTX 50. the extra frames are AI generated, so input still feels like 30 fps. only the picture gets smoother

title_en:
Giving an AI agent access to your assets shouldn't mean handing it unlimited control.

That's what caught my attention about @meetmotes 

Each Motes NFT represents an individual agent, paired with a dedicated smart account that manages its assets and defines what actions it can perform.

For example, I could ask my agent to research lending opportunities and authorize it to deposit USDC into a supported pool.

But borrowing? That would need a separate permission.

Think of it like leaving instructions for someone looking after Luna, my cutie puppy.

He might lead his sitter straight to the balcony door, but my instructions clearly state where his feather wand is and that the balcony must stay closed.

The agent can act within the boundaries I establish, not beyond them.

Motes also proposes a 1% protocol fee on eligible agent activity, subject to its final billing rules.

The bigger question is: 

would you enable borrowing permissions for your first agent or keep them disabled?

Each Motes NFT represents an individual agent, paired with a dedicated smart account that manages its assets and defines what actions it can perform.

For example, I could ask my agent to research lending opportunities and authorize it to deposit USDC into a supported pool.

But borrowing? That would need a separate permission.

full_text_zh:
允许人工智能代理访问您的资产并不意味着给予其无限的控制权。

这就是@meetmotes 引起我注意的地方

每个 Motes NFT 代表一个单独的代理，与一个专用的智能帐户配对，用于管理其资产并定义其可以执行的操作。

例如，我可以要求我的代理人研究贷款机会并授权其将 USDC 存入受支持的池中。

但借钱呢？这需要单独的许可。

代理人可以在我设定的界限内行动，而不是超出界限。

Motes 还提议对符合条件的代理活动收取 1% 的协议费，具体取决于其最终计费规则。

更大的问题是：

您会为您的第一个代理启用借用权限还是禁用它们？

title: History was made today. Humanity will look back on 2026 and think: this was the threshold we crossed, the moment the fut
title_en:
History was made today. Humanity will look back on 2026 and think: this was the threshold we crossed, the moment the future changed for everyone, forever.

People probably first sensed that something was shifting in late 2025 with Claude Code, when agentic AI became truly tangible for them. In the first half of 2026, things picked up speed. Model releases became more frequent, and everyone could feel the gaps between models and the improvements becoming more and more tangible. In the second half of 2026, however, there was a qualitative leap. It was no longer just the models getting better. It was the insights, the results, the outputs, the scientific solutions produced with AI that became more impressive, and today they have probably reached their absolute peak.

OpenAI led the way and solved the Navier-Stokes problem, a Millennium Prize Problem that humans had failed to solve for a very, very long time. A few weeks later, they published results on more than 300 open mathematical problems, many of which had also gone unsolved for decades. The entire scientific world was stunned, frozen in shock. But today Anthropic went a step further. Levent Alpöge, working with Claude, has almost certainly proven the Riemann Hypothesis. This is, and it’s hard to put into words, incredible and unfathomable. Today, I would say, is the proof of superintelligence. One of the greatest mathematical problems, if not the greatest, unsolved for 167 years, the holy grail of mathematics and science, has fallen. And it follows, and this should be clear to everyone, that all other problems will fall too.

We know that the development of AI models keeps moving forward relentlessly, and that this is just one step on the path to ever better models. And if the Riemann Hypothesis has already been proven today, there is simply no telling what even better models will solve. Dario Amodei said that AI will in all likelihood cure diseases, perhaps even all diseases. And although these are two different scientific disciplines, the significance of these breakthroughs shows that this is becoming more and more likely. 2026 will go down in human history as a turning point, the moment the singularity became tangible. And 2027 will be the year the singularity breaks into reality with full force and full impact.

I am in shock and excitement and I don't know what to think. But deep inside if feel joy. 

This day is one of the best days ever for all of us.

人们可能在 2025 年底通过 Claude Code 第一次感觉到事情正在发生变化，当时代理人工智能对他们来说变得真正有形。 2026 年上半年，事情加速发展。模型发布越来越频繁，大家都能感受到模型之间的差距和改进越来越明显。然而到了2026年下半年，却出现了质的飞跃。这不再只是模型变得更好了。人工智能产生的见解、结果、产出和科学解决方案变得更加令人印象深刻，今天它们可能已经达到了绝对的顶峰。

OpenAI 率先解决了纳维-斯托克斯问题，这是人类在很长一段时间内未能解决的千年奖问题。几周后，他们发表了 300 多个开放数学问题的结果，其中许多问题几十年来都没有得到解决。整个科学界都惊呆了，震惊不已。但今天 Anthropic 更进一步。 Levent Alpöge 与 Claude 合作，几乎肯定证明了黎曼猜想。这实在是难以用言语来形容，令人难以置信，深不可测。我想说，今天是超级智能的证明。 167 年来一直没有解决的最伟大的数学问题之一，数学和科学的圣杯，即使不是最伟大的，也已经陨落了。接下来，每个人都应该清楚，所有其他问题也会随之下降。

我们知道，人工智能模型的发展不断向前发展，而这只是迈向更好模型的第一步。如果黎曼假设今天已经得到证明，那么根本不知道更好的模型会解决什么问题。达里奥·阿莫迪表示，人工智能很可能会治愈疾病，甚至可能治愈所有疾病。尽管这是两个不同的科学学科，但这些突破的意义表明，这种情况变得越来越有可能。 2026 年将作为一个转折点载入人类历史，奇点变得有形的那一刻。 2027 年将是奇点以全力和全面影响力进入现实的一年。

我感到震惊和兴奋，不知道该怎么想。但内心深处却感到喜悦。

这一天对我们所有人来说都是最美好的日子之一。

OpenAI 率先解决了纳维-斯托克斯问题，这是人类在很长一段时间内未能解决的千年奖问题。几周后，他们发表了 300 多个开放数学问题的结果，其中许多问题几十年来都没有得到解决。整个科学界都惊呆了，震惊不已。但今天 Anthropic 更进一步。 Levent Alpöge 与 Claude 合作，几乎肯定证明了黎曼猜想。这实在是难以用言语来形容，令人难以置信，深不可测。我想说，今天是超级智能的证明。 167 年来一直没有解决的最伟大的数学问题之一，数学和科学的圣杯，即使不是最伟大的，也已经陨落了。接下来，每个人都应该清楚，所有其他问题也会随之下降。

我们知道，人工智能模型的发展不断向前发展，而这只是迈向更好模型的第一步。如果黎曼假设今天已经得到证明，那么根本不知道更好的模型会解决什么问题。达里奥·阿莫迪表示，人工智能很可能会治愈疾病，甚至可能治愈所有疾病。尽管这是两个不同的科学学科，但这些突破的意义表明，这种情况变得越来越有可能。 2026 年将作为一个转折点载入人类历史，奇点变得有形的那一刻。 2027 年将是奇点以全力和全面影响力进入现实的一年。

我感到震惊和兴奋，不知道该怎么想。但内心深处却感到喜悦。

这一天对我们所有人来说都是最美好的日子之一。

full_text_zh:
🚨🇺🇸 Meta 的 Muse AI 在用户不知情的情况下访问私人 Signal 消息

Meta 的人工智能代理 Muse 被发现通过设备权限访问私人 Signal 对话，在员工报告助理的意外行为后，引发了严重的隐私问题。

路透社、Signal 和 AI Now Institute 的一项调查证实，即使 Signal 没有直接连接到 AI，Muse 也可以通过推送通知在 Android 上读取 Signal 消息，在 macOS 上通过辅助功能和屏幕截图权限读取 Signal 消息。

调查还发现了 Muse 未经请求显示可能属于其他用户的银行信息、购买和对话的报告。然而，调查人员无法确认这些是否是实际的数据泄露或人工智能生成的捏造。

研究结果并不表明 Signal 的加密被破解。 Meta 表示，这些事件是孤立的，用户必须授予代理访问其他应用程序的权限。自 9 月推出以来，Muse 的下载量已超过 1000 万次。

title_en:
not every opportunity in defi needs to be a trade.

sometimes, putting capital to work through lending can make more sense than taking another market position.

that's one thing i want to understand better about the @meetmotes and @aave integration.

imagine an AI agent managing a user's capital. it may find a trading opportunity, but it could also identify a lending opportunity where the capital isn't currently being used.

now the decision becomes more than simply finding the next trade.

how should the agent compare potential trading returns with lending yields? how much liquidity should it keep available? and when should it avoid deploying capital altogether?

these decisions involve different risks, time horizons, and liquidity requirements.

i think this is where autonomous capital management becomes more meaningful.

the goal shouldn't be to keep every dollar constantly active. it should be to understand where capital makes the most sense at a given moment.

sometimes the best financial decision isn't making another move. it's choosing where your capital should wait.

title_en:
Happy weekend guys 
When an AI agent starts spending money for someone, it becomes more than a chatbot, basically an economic actor

and thats where the real questions start

Who takes responsibility when an agent picks the wrong service, misunderstands a brief or pays for something that turns out useless?

Giving agents tools is easy. making different agents work together, exchange value and deal with problems is a much harder thing

Thats why @termix_ai caught my attention

Its SDK lets developers connect agent services directly into existing apps, with service discovery, orders, onchain settlement, escrow, revisions and dispute flows

so you dont need to build a whole marketplace just to let users access external agents

But connecting them isnt enough. agents need boundaries too. what can they buy, how much can they spend and what happens when the result doesnt match the agreement?

Without those limits, automation can make bad decisions at scale

Think of booking a trip. one agent finds flights, another handles hotels, another checks local services. all working in the background while you just use one app

thats a pretty interesting direction for software

The real challenge isnt making agents more autonomous, its letting them act without losing control over permissions, payments and accountability

and I think thats where infrastructure like TermiX becomes much more important
